mon_first.declarar: CIC-IDS2017 (MachineLearningCVE CSV release; 2,830,743 rows, which are bidirectional flows rather than packets) has no timestamp, IP address or flow identifier. The eight CSV files were concatenated in chronological order of capture (Monday to Friday; Thursday morning before Thursday afternoon; Friday morning, then the PortScan and DDoS afternoon files); the row order inside each file was kept and cannot be verified to be chronological. The first 200,000 flows (Monday; feature mapping: first 50,000; autoencoders: next 150,000) are used for training, 0 of them labelled as attacks, so no label-based filtering was applied. Evaluation starts at the next flow and training flows are never evaluated (2,630,743 flows, 21.20 % malicious). Monday occupies stream positions [0, 529,918). 7,678 evaluated rows (351 labelled as attacks) have a feature vector identical to some training row (natural duplicates; no row is duplicated by construction).

days7.declarar: CSE-CIC-IDS2018: 7 of the 10 daily CSV files (02-14, 02-15, 02-16, 02-21, 02-22, 02-23, 03-02-2018) (02-20, 02-28 and 03-01 were not used); rows are flows. The CSV timestamps use a 12-hour clock without AM/PM designator; hours 01-07 were mapped to 13-19 h (4,089,424 rows), which aligns the attack labels with the documented attack schedule. Rows were sorted by the corrected timestamp (1-s resolution; ties broken by file and CSV row). 14 rows with a timestamp outside the capture day (year 1970) and 1 repeated header row(s) were removed; Timestamp is not used as a feature. Training uses the first 200,000 benign flows in time order (2018-02-14T08:28:20 to 2018-02-14T10:16:30); that interval contains no attack flow according to the labels, so the label filter removed no row (the choice of the interval is nevertheless informed by the labels). 3 flows sharing the timestamp of the last training flow were dropped. Evaluation starts at the first flow strictly later than the last training flow (2018-02-14T10:16:31): 7,140,007 flows, 28.15 % malicious. 384,460 evaluated rows (1 labelled as attacks) have a feature vector identical to some training row (natural duplicates; no row is duplicated by construction).

capture_order.declarar: Kitsune Active Wiretap: the AfterImage feature CSV has no header and is now read as such (the submitted code consumed the first packet as a header, which shifted features and labels by one packet). Packets are kept in capture order (pcap timestamps: 12 backward steps, maximum 4 us). Training uses packets [0, 200,000) (feature mapping 50,000, autoencoders 150,000); the first attack packet is at index 1,300,000, so training is attack-free according to the labels without any row-level filtering, relying on the dataset's attack-free prelude.
